decisions.decision: Ship the pinned Metal runtime’s existing Q8_0 attention cache with explicit precision control and FP16 fallback. This is not an implementation of KIVI, TurboQuant, or UltraQuant. Those papers motivate cache compression; their bits, kernels, devices, and results do not transfer to this app. Q8_0 stores 34 bytes for 32 values versus 64 FP16 bytes. Total memory savings depend on the architecture and workload. Automatic selection is conservative for recurrent/sliding-window architectures: ordinary fitting chats keep FP16; Q8 is considered for longer contexts or to make a requested window fit. Dense models use Q8 when estimated cache savings exceed 256 MiB. Reviewed Gemma 4 and Qwen3.5 cache geometry now determines meaningful savings: shared layers, bounded sliding windows and FP32 recurrent state are accounted for separately. Two partial-state checkpoints are reserved in estimates and explicitly enforced by the runtime flags.

Already available through the existing runtime. Explicitly require its supported path for quantized V cache and retain auto mode for full precision. Do not claim this is a newly invented kernel or FlashAttention-3 CUDA performance on Metal.

Offer budgeted contexts up to 65536 tokens, never beyond pinned model metadata. Preserve publisher-provided runtime parameters; do not force arbitrary RoPE scaling. Add synthetic long-input retrieval with exact tokenizer accounting, separate from capacity claims.

decisions.technique: Speculative decoding, EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark, MTP
decisions.decision: Investigated but not enabled globally. Model-specific drafting heads/checkpoints, additional memory, acceptance rates and workload matter. N-gram speculation needs measured benefit across ordinary chat, not only repetitive code; none is claimed here.

decisions.technique: Prefix reuse and bounded history preparation
decisions.decision: Retain in-memory matching prefix reuse with auxiliary RAM archive disabled. Replace linear turn-by-turn context trimming with exact-tokenizer bisection over complete-turn boundaries. Never silently summarize, overwrite, or train on user chat.
Not a direct win for Hearth’s single-user single-slot runtime. Do not import server batching complexity or claim a new model intelligence gain.

decisions.technique: Architecture-aware cache planning and bounded checkpoints
decisions.decision: Compute shared/sliding/recurrent storage from pinned metadata for reviewed architectures. Bound partial-state checkpoints to two instead of 32. Keep unknown layouts conservative and preserve FP32 recurrent state. The cache layout itself is provided by the existing runtime; Hearth now budgets it correctly.
